notes: Goal planning opens with your plan at a glance: the extra needed a month, goals on track, what's set aside and retirement, then tabs for Goals and Retirement
Goals show as cards with a progress bar and the next step, and each goal's details open full screen with its figures as cards
Retirement leads with when your money runs out, a timeline of working, retired and any years not covered, ways to close a gap as cards, and one chart at a time
Your assumptions are grouped into You, Spending, Investing and After you retire, with the key numbers shown when folded
Set each investment: each shows what it does after you retire, and opens to edit with a plain explanation, how it pays, then the amount
The bottom tab bar is solid, and content fades out above it instead of showing through
Payouts that vary, such as a profit share or dividends, can be set up with just how often they come; Home asks for the amount each time, and it's added to income and counted in returns
Any investment can now pay out to your bank, and the category page shows Payouts received

Tapping an investment category opens its own page: value and gain first, a growth chart of value against invested (6M, 1Y, 3Y, All), the split by holding, each holding with its actions, and recent activity
Market-linked holdings show absolute return and CAGR beside XIRR
Deposits, bonds and similar can pay interest out monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly; each payout shows on Home to mark as received, is added to income, and counts towards returns
Each category shows interest received, all time and this financial year, and holdings have an Interest button for payouts off the schedule
Adding an investment opens one form with the type, owner and payout as tappable choices instead of dropdowns, in short sections
Fixed deposits, bonds, PF and PPF show their interest rate, and no-return holdings their absolute return, instead of XIRR, in each holding's details and on Analytics
Home's cards no longer change shape after visiting Plan
Plan's overview shows your retirement planner's result: on course or how much short, with on course against needed
Money: tap the month name on the balance card to pick a month, or swipe the card; the month row and search box are gone
Home drops the quick actions row, as the + in the tab bar does the same, and the asset allocation card on Wealth is shorter on phones
Wealth: You own (with your return) beside You owe (with your debt-free date), the asset pie on phones, chips under it, and Stallion PMS in the investment list
Holdings show as compact rows with a six-month trend line, and loans with their progress, under Wealth
Each loan's details have buttons for EMI payment, part payment, rate change, top-up and revised EMI, each opening its form
Plan opens with retirement as a ring, your other goals as tiles, and a growth projection preview
Home: wider cards on phones, For you today below the month with shorter cards, and smaller quick actions
Money lists entries without daily totals, each with its date, so more fit on screen
Money: months as pills you tap or swipe, the balance with one split bar, and See where it went for the full flow
Wealth: what you own after what you owe, your investment mix, and chips for investments, retirement and loans
A new look: four tabs (Home, Money, Wealth, Plan) in a floating bar, with a big + in the middle for adding anything
Home: net worth with a chart you can switch between 1M, 6M, 1Y and All, quick actions, swipeable For you today cards, this month as a ring, what's coming up and your latest entries
Money: search the month's entries and filter by category; on phones entries are grouped by day, with icons for common categories
Wealth: net worth, what you own and owe, and a switch between investments and loans
Plan opens on an overview of your goals, this year's budget and every planning tool

Cash flow is one card: the month's balance, then where the money went as a flow, with income sources merging into one total and splitting into spending, unrecorded spending, loan EMIs, investing and the balance, each with its amount and share. On a computer spending splits into its categories too; on a phone, tap a band for details. It's shorter, so Add income or expense shows without scrolling

Settings redesigned: your profile on top, then grouped lists (General, Family & security, Your data, Help, About) with one tap to each setting, and Sign out at the end. Reminders, Security, Send feedback and Share the app now have rows of their own

Dashboard: this month's income, expenses, savings and balance in one shorter card, each with a small six-month trend line and how it compares with last month. Spending compares with the same day last month. Tap a figure to open it

Loan EMIs and part payments are no longer counted as spending: they repay debt, so Expenses, the charts and the month recap show them on their own. Mark a loan as a lifestyle EMI, such as a phone bought on EMI, and its EMIs count as spending. Balances still take them off
Debts on phones: loan cards drop the Active label, and the summary header fits on one line
Investments on phones: the allocation chart sits above a two-column key, so names don't wrap
Yearly budget: a line can count spending in several categories, such as Grocery, Milk and Fruits together
Budget vs actual, in Planning › Insights: pick a planned year and see what you spent against it, by month and by category, plus spending that isn't in the plan
Yearly budget: use it for spending only, or add the income you expect (monthly or yearly) to see income vs budget and what's left to invest. Income recorded so far is no longer used
Yearly budget, in Planning › Future: plan the financial year line by line, monthly, yearly, in chosen months or once
A starting plan filled in from your last twelve months of spending, with school fees added for each kid
See what each month needs and which months need more than you set aside, how spending is going against the plan, and what's left to invest
Big yearly bills due this month or next show in Needs attention
Copy a year's plan to the next, with prices and school fees up by the percent you choose
Planning is split into Insights (Analytics, Income, Date range reports) and Future (Growth projection, Goal planning, Yearly budget)
Monthly balances no longer repeat the unrecorded house expense, which the month summary already shows
Data health in Settings: what would make your figures wrong, with a fix for each
Cash flow spots expenses that repeat each month and offers to make them recurring
Year at a glance in Date range reports, with a PDF for tax time
Opens faster on a first visit, and every page passes accessibility checks
Cash flow on phones: tap the month name to pick any month, in place of the dropdown at the top
The month summary is shorter, so more of the page fits on screen
Cash flow on phones: the month reads as a flow from income to balance, with one bar showing where it went
Swipe the month summary, or tap the arrows, to move between months
On phones the portfolio sort sits beside its title
Cash flow shows what you invested from income, and the balance after spending and investing
A forgotten expense added after a month is reviewed is no longer counted twice
Cash flow shows the month's unrecorded house expense as its own figure, the same before and after review
The financial year label no longer breaks across lines
Monthly Expenses and Available Balance on the dashboard no longer change when a month is reviewed
Gratuity opens to edit the basic salary or delete, both inside its details
Retirement planner: the second chart shows yearly spending, tappable by age, and both charts sit side by side on a computer
On a computer the dashboard shows up to eight investments, lines up the chart and portfolio, and the goals tile is shorter
Today's insights: ten a day, anything needing action first, fresh picks each morning
Eleven new insights, from how long your bank balance lasts to PPF room left, saving streaks and when you'll be debt-free
The income chart shows six months everywhere, and on a computer sits beside your portfolio with a pie of where last month's income went
The dashboard chart starts from your first month of income or spending, and investments entered for earlier months no longer count as invested from income
EMI reminders can be marked as paid in one tap, which records the EMI, or hidden for the month
An EMI whose due date passed with nothing recorded is flagged, so a hidden or forgotten one isn't missed
Tablets keep the bottom tab bar, and the top bar fits from 1024px wide with short labels, full ones from 1180px
The retirement planner responds faster while you type, especially on phones
Retirement assumptions end with Save and close, which saves, folds them away and takes you back to the results
A card scrolled into view stops below the header instead of under it
Retirement planner: "What you'll need" is never rosier than your own plan, so its "On course for" matches your fund at retirement when your rates are the cautious ones
The rates it uses are spelt out, such as "8% growth before retiring, 10% after"
Retirement planner: an income investment's payout can be a rupee amount paid monthly, quarterly or yearly, as well as a percentage a year
Retirement assumptions stay open while you type, instead of closing once an error clears
Opening a wide table, such as investment returns details or the retirement year-by-year, no longer makes the page scroll sideways
The saved unrecorded house expense is titled by its category, with a note that it came from the month review
Marking a month reviewed saves its unrecorded house expense as an expense entry, and reviewing again updates or removes it
Unrecorded house expense, what your closing balance falls short of, now counts as spending on the dashboard, in Analytics, goals and the retirement planner
The month close takes off everything invested from your bank, so SIPs and PPF are no longer counted as house expense
Add a forgotten expense later and the unrecorded part shrinks, so nothing is counted twice
The dashboard chart's investing bar shows only what you invested from income; PF and NPS, taken from salary first, are left out
Dashboard chart shows income against expenses, with each month's investing stacked on top
Dashboard on a computer: net worth beside this month's figures, and the expense snapshot tile is removed
Retirement planner reads more easily: matching headline tiles, figures lined up, and more room between lines
Retirement charts: your fund by age, and after retiring, what the fund makes against what you spend, with when it starts to shrink
Retirement assumptions sit two to a row, and each investment's settings are compact
A rate left blank asks for a figure instead of counting as 0%
Retirement planner: set each investment after retiring to grow, pay income, or both
Income investments such as SCSS or an FD keep their value and pay your spending first, before anything is sold
At retirement, move a share of an investment into an income investment, and mark what can't be sold, such as an annuity
The graph and year-by-year table show payouts alongside what is sold
PF, PPF and NPS show as one row each in goal funding and investment returns, instead of account numbers
Retirement table shows months only on part years, such as the year you retire in
Retirement planner runs from this month by financial year, retires in your exact month, and marks the retirement milestone
Income tab: salary against other income, each source and how often it comes
Salary over time with raises found for you, and this year against last year
Who earns what, how steady your income is, where each ₹100 goes, and savings rate by month
Income insights on the dashboard
Reports is now called Planning, as it holds analysis, goals and the retirement planner
Retirement planner in Goal planning: your fund at retirement, spending then, and how long the money lasts
A graph of fund value and yearly expenses by age, with a year-by-year table
What you will need at realistic rates, the gap, and the monthly investing that closes it
Date of birth and retirement date, with your age shown at each step
Goal and planner amounts read in lakhs and crores
Portfolio targets use your savings contributions, the same figure as the dashboard, counted from when you started tracking
Goal planning has its own page in Reports, next to Growth Projection
Portfolio targets count your investing only from when you started tracking
The older portfolio goal planner is replaced by the portfolio target goal
Portfolio target predicts from what you invest each month, and shows how much sooner investing what is left over would be
Long goal names and the portfolio sort now fit on small phones
Portfolio target: aim for a net worth or investment amount, and see when you will reach it
The prediction uses your average income less spending, loan repayments and growth, with each figure shown
Goals: save for education, a house, retirement and more, funded from a share of your investments
Each goal says whether you are on track, and how much more a month gets you there
What-if sliders for each goal, a goals tile on the dashboard, and goal insights and celebrations
Retirement and emergency fund goals suggest a target from your own spending
A brighter aurora behind every page, in your chosen colours
Your net worth leads the dashboard, with the recap and install prompts as slim one-line cards below your figures
Debts opens with what is left to repay, how much is paid and when you will be debt-free
Reports list each record with its amount on phones, 20 at a time
Amounts from ₹1 crore show in crores, and retirement funds chart by type
A softer aurora background, smoother header and turning chevrons on fold-outs
The dashboard opens with your greeting, and Needs attention stands out with a bell and a count
Monthly figures have colour-coded icons, and nothing recorded yet shows as Not yet
Active loans are marked in mint, and the trend chart bars have a soft fade
A fresher look: the Net Worth tile glows mint, and every tile has a mint edge
Insights is now a tidy tile on the dashboard: tap to open, with the top one as a preview
This month's investing, loan principal repaid and PMS gain now appear as insights
Insights on your dashboard: patterns in your money, worked out privately on your phone
A monthly recap of income, spending, savings and net worth
More of the screen on phones: a slimmer space under the tab bar, set for iPhone and Android
The bottom tab bar is solid and sits lower on iPhone
